The provided evidence explicitly confirms this in Section 3.2: 'For efficient rendering of the clusters of grid cells in our data structure, we replace the vertex shader of previous approaches with a tesselation shader taking a single patch (GL_PATCHES primitive) per cluster as input and expands it into points for the cells in the cluster.' It also confirms the context of isosurface rendering and the use of point sprites (billboards) for rasterization.

The claim states that the evidence supports the detection of isosurface intersection where f(p) = tau. Source [S1] explicitly describes a rendering technique (Cell Rasterisation) where 'the original volume data is sampled along the ray with tri-linear interpolation to find isosurface intersections.' It further details that 'interpolated samples... computed along the ray to determine the isosurface intersection.' In volume rendering, finding an isosurface intersection inherently involves finding the point p where the scalar field value f(p) equals the specified threshold tau. The evidence confirms that this specific operation is performed by the technique described.
